episodes.title: What is an MIS, really?
episodes.thesis: An MIS is one record per person, shared by everyone, that the work runs through.

episodes.title: Why nonprofits struggle with data even after buying software
episodes.thesis: The gap is process clarity and ownership, not tools.

episodes.title: Why 80% placement isn't 80% employment
episodes.thesis: Placement is a leading indicator; retention is the outcome that matters.

episodes.title: Should your nonprofit build, buy or customise software?
episodes.thesis: Decide on process clarity, capacity and uniqueness, not on features.

episodes.title: Why dashboards don't automatically improve decisions
episodes.thesis: A dashboard without a decision is decoration.

episodes.title: Every field is a tax on the frontline
episodes.thesis: Every data point must earn its place; more data is not better.

episodes.title: If data only flows up, it's compliance
episodes.thesis: Data must flow back to the people who enter it.

episodes.title: Theory of Change in five minutes
episodes.thesis: Activities, outputs, outcomes, impact: the causal story behind a programme.

episodes.title: What a logframe is for, and why funders ask for it
episodes.thesis: The Theory of Change is the story; the logframe is the matrix.

episodes.title: Outputs vs outcomes: the indicator trap
episodes.thesis: Counting what you did is not the same as measuring change.

episodes.title: Leading and lagging indicators: attendance vs income
episodes.thesis: Early signals let you act before the outcome is lost.

episodes.title: What one unique ID actually fixes
episodes.thesis: One stable ID per person ends duplicates and conflicting counts.

episodes.title: A single source of truth isn't one file
episodes.thesis: It is an agreement: one definition, one ID, one owner per concept.

episodes.title: Go-live is the start line
episodes.thesis: Adoption begins at go-live; plan for the months after.

episodes.title: Why staff stop using new systems
episodes.thesis: Adoption is a social process, not a technical event.

episodes.title: Don't automate a messy kitchen
episodes.thesis: Automate a confused workflow and you get a confused workflow at scale.

episodes.title: Technology has three jobs. Do them in order.
episodes.thesis: Infrastructure, then acceleration, then insight.

episodes.title: Mission-rich, systems-poor
episodes.thesis: Nonprofits are rich in purpose and short on systems; the gap is structural.

episodes.title: Problem first, tool last
episodes.thesis: Tools feel like progress; problems feel like delay.

episodes.title: A free tool nobody uses isn't free
episodes.thesis: The cost of software is mostly the cost of making it stick.

episodes.title: Why a prototype that fails in week two is a gift
episodes.thesis: Early mismatch is cheap; late mismatch is expensive.

episodes.title: Stop rebuilding the same system
episodes.thesis: Sector patterns repeat; start from them.

episodes.title: Built for donors, not teams
episodes.thesis: Systems designed only for compliance fail the frontline.

episodes.title: 'We have a data problem' usually isn't
episodes.thesis: It is usually a decision, workflow or adoption problem.

episodes.title: Baseline, midline, endline: measuring change
episodes.thesis: Measure the same thing before, during and after.

episodes.title: Red, amber, green: making targets readable
episodes.thesis: Thresholds turn numbers into decisions.

episodes.title: The three maps of any nonprofit: people, money, evidence
episodes.thesis: Show how people, money and evidence move, and where they meet.

episodes.title: What India's DPDP Act means for nonprofit data
episodes.thesis: Consent, purpose and minimisation become legal duties.

episodes.title: Consent: the field you can't skip
episodes.thesis: Consent is a record with a date, a purpose and a way to withdraw.

episodes.title: Is your organisation ready for a new system?
episodes.thesis: Leadership buy-in, process clarity and realistic sequencing come first.

episodes.title: How AI voice agents actually work
episodes.thesis: Speech to text to understanding to the next question, with a human in the loop.

episodes.title: What is an AI employee, and how is it different from a chatbot?
episodes.thesis: A chatbot answers; an AI employee does an encoded task end to end, with review.

episodes.title: AI is an amplifier, not a purifier
episodes.thesis: AI on messy data produces confident mess.

episodes.title: The AI maturity ladder: from chatbot to organisation-wide
episodes.thesis: Climb one rung at a time: chat, file in/deliverable out, encoded task, scheduled, organisation-wide.

episodes.title: What a data model is: entities, fields, relationships
episodes.thesis: Decide the things you track, what you know about them and how they connect.

episodes.title: One-to-many, many-to-many: how records connect
episodes.thesis: Relationships stop you copying the same data into many places.

episodes.title: Master tables: why dropdowns matter
episodes.thesis: Standard lists make counts comparable.

episodes.title: Reading an entity-relationship diagram
episodes.thesis: Boxes are things; lines are how they relate.

episodes.title: Moving off spreadsheets: data migration without tears
episodes.thesis: Clean, map, test, then move; never migrate the mess.

episodes.title: What user acceptance testing is for
episodes.thesis: UAT is where real users prove the system fits real work.

episodes.title: How systems talk to each other: APIs in plain words
episodes.thesis: Systems share data through agreed requests, not copy and paste.

episodes.title: Collecting data where there's no internet
episodes.thesis: Capture offline, sync later, resolve conflicts deliberately.

episodes.title: Why duplicates happen, and how systems prevent them
episodes.thesis: Duplicates come from many entry points and no shared ID.

episodes.title: Validation rules: stopping bad data at the door
episodes.thesis: Rules at entry are cheaper than cleaning later.

episodes.title: Who sees what: roles and permissions
episodes.thesis: Least privilege protects people and the data about them.

episodes.title: Audit trails: who changed what, and when
episodes.thesis: Trust in data comes from knowing its history.

episodes.title: Collecting stories at scale: qualitative data
episodes.thesis: Conversations capture the why behind the numbers.

episodes.title: Where AI fits in a nonprofit MIS
episodes.thesis: Collect, build, work smarter, know faster, on trusted data only.

episodes.title: Why we build on low-code platforms
episodes.thesis: Speed, ownership and cost of change matter more than custom code.

episodes.title: Inside ImpactOS: how we build an MIS
episodes.thesis: A structured path from discovery to adoption.

episodes.title: MAP: model, align, power with AI
episodes.thesis: Model what is worth knowing, align with real work, add AI on trusted data.

episodes.title: Why we tell prospects what we can't do
episodes.thesis: Honesty about readiness saves everyone a failed project.

episodes.title: When the project hits a wall
episodes.thesis: A blocker protocol beats blame.

episodes.title: Warmth is how standards travel
episodes.thesis: High standards spread through relationships.

episodes.title: How Zolabs turns a survey into a conversation
episodes.thesis: A voice conversation collects richer, more honest answers than a form.

episodes.title: How DozAI verifies placement and retention
episodes.thesis: Bounded AI follow-ups with human review. Confirm framing with the product owner first.

episodes.title: ISOM: an open operating model for skilling nonprofits
episodes.thesis: Shared stages and SOPs so every skilling nonprofit need not start from zero.

episodes.title: What happens in a discovery call
episodes.thesis: We ask about your Theory of Change before any tool.

episodes.title: The patterns we see across 16 sectors
episodes.thesis: Every sector has one data thread that holds it together.

episodes.title: How we make these videos
episodes.thesis: Structured storyboards, open tools and human review.
